sections.heading: The buying case: Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red
paragraphs: The Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT is a credible first complete RWD drift purchase for somebody who wants a finished modern coupe and coordinated steering assistance before exploring electronics upgrades. Its useful feature is not simply a red Toyota shell: the D2 is a drift-specific rear-drive chassis with a receiver/gyro arrangement that can influence steering and throttle. My reservation is that a casual Readyset should still be checked against the tires, equipment and expectations of your intended drift venue.

The exact reviewed car is Lightning Red 34502T1, verified by Amazon under that same part number. It is not an ordinary 4WD Fazer fitted with slippery tires, a bare D2 chassis kit, a replacement GT86 body or the AE86 sibling. Those products can appear in related searches and lead to different completion costs. The supplied body and radio installation make this a complete assembled car, while the drive battery, charger and transmitter cells remain separate purchases.

I would shortlist it for learning circles and linked turns on smooth ground, especially when you prefer a coordinated beginner package to choosing separate radio, gyro and servo components. The editorial rating concerns that purchasing brief. We have not drifted the car, compared tandem pace or measured its control response. A manufacturer's promise of accessible drifting remains a manufacturer claim, and local track advice is the useful next check for a buyer seeking regular club sessions.

sections.heading: The complete package: Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red
paragraphs: The Readyset contains a completed chassis, painted and decorated body, fitted motor and controller, receiver with built-in gyro, steering servo and Syncro KT-231P+ transmitter. Kyosho names the KRG-331D receiver and KS4072-06W servo. Tools and setting-change parts are listed. That reduces the integration work which would be required if you bought a chassis and then selected every drift electronic separately.

You need four AA transmitter cells, a suitable drive battery and compatible charger. The exact product page recommends a 7.2 V NiMH route and names specific SPEED HOUSE packs and chargers. If you prefer another battery chemistry, check the current controller manual, connector and physical holder arrangement rather than assuming every D2 listing or creator video settles that choice. A pack’s capacity alone does not establish compatibility or fit.

Before the first session, check steering travel and wheel attachment, read the gyro and transmitter instructions and establish the documented stock settings. Inspect the paint and body mounting without turning setup into a modification project. The purpose of the Readyset is to begin with a coordinated baseline, not to imply that no control checks are necessary. I would have the correct charged pack ready, preserve the original adjustment positions in notes and start on a surface where an inconsistent slide is unlikely to end against a curb.

sections.heading: Drivetrain and power: Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red
paragraphs: Only the rear wheels are driven. The D2's high-mounted motor and drift-specific weight distribution distinguish it from the general Fazer touring arrangement. Kyosho lists a brushed G22 motor, 9.1:1 overall ratio and plastic drift tires. Those establish a coherent casual-drift package. They do not prove a particular throttle feel, wheel speed or advantage over sensored-brushless competition electronics.

The practical appeal of RWD is learning the relationship between rear-wheel traction, throttle and countersteering. It is a different discipline from an AWD touring car sliding with all four wheels powered. An attractive body cannot bridge that difference. If your intended venue expects RWD, this package starts in the correct broad category, but the track's tire and setup requirements still need checking. If it expects a specific motor or controller system, stock brushed equipment becomes a real purchase consideration.

I would use the supplied power system long enough to establish whether the overall package suits the intended practice. An immediate motor, controller, radio and servo replacement can erase the Readyset’s value advantage. The manufacturer’s motor mount supports pinion changes, but that flexibility is not a recommendation to raise gearing before the first drift. Learn a repeatable stock maneuver, monitor the car according to the manual and change one item only after identifying the reason. This review supplies no measured temperature, speed or runtime number for that configuration.

sections.heading: Radio and setup: Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red
paragraphs: The KRG-331D’s built-in gyro can moderate both steering and throttle. Kyosho documents separate sensitivity adjustments, so it is important to understand that assistance is not restricted to moving the front wheels. A buyer who wants traditional steering-only gyro behavior should read the D2 instructions carefully and establish which adjustments match the intended driving style. The system is a tool to learn, not evidence that any surface will automatically produce a controlled slide.

The KT-231P+ offers steering/throttle trims and steering dual rate in the documented package. Set neutral positions and check the controller startup procedure before driving. Change only one assistance adjustment between attempts, keeping tire and ground conditions constant. If the car suddenly behaves differently after a tire or surface change, return to the recorded baseline before deciding the gyro is the sole cause.

Big Squid RC’s Toyota86 D2 announcement identifies the same subject with a regional B suffix. It is release coverage, not an independent drive test of our exact T1 Amazon offer. The source supports attributed context about the new drift-specific package without supplying a reliability record or measured control result. Greg Vogel’s AE86 D2 driving coverage is about another body variant and is not carried across as a Toyota86 test. These distinctions keep the buying assessment useful without allowing related videos to become evidence of performance we have not measured.

sections.heading: Steering and suspension: Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red
paragraphs: The drift-specific chassis incorporates long suspension arms and a steering arrangement intended for substantial countersteer. Kyosho identifies a dedicated servo working with the gyro. Those are meaningful package facts for a first RWD drifter. They are not permission to print an unverified maximum steering-angle number or guarantee that the car will recover every large slide. Mechanical range, endpoints, tire contact and assistance need to work together.

With the car powered according to its instructions, sweep the steering gently and watch for a wheel or linkage meeting a stop while the servo continues to push. Use the documented transmitter settings and avoid treating maximum travel as the only desirable setup. A tire touching the body or a linkage binding at the end of movement should be investigated physically, not hidden under a bigger steering command.

The chassis has a 260 mm stock wheelbase and a documented 240–274 mm adjustment range. Changing wheelbase for another shell is a mechanical configuration project involving body fit and clearances; it is not a reason to replace the finished Toyota86 immediately. Keep the standard geometry for initial practice and make notes when changing alignment. We assess the documented adjustment possibilities as ownership tools. There is no measured claim here that one wheelbase or geometry setting will give your track more grip or make tandem running easier.

sections.heading: Where to drive: Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red
paragraphs: This is a smooth-ground drift car. The plastic drift tires and approximately 12 mm chassis height explain why grass, gravel and jumps are outside the sensible purchase brief. Find clean pavement or a suitable indoor drift surface with room for repeated circles. Loose grit and raised edges can interrupt a slide abruptly. The floor is part of the setup, not merely the place where the car happens to sit.

If you plan to visit a drift club, confirm the required tire before buying extra sets. A venue may standardize grip and pace with a prescribed tire. The supplied plastic tire is a starting configuration, not proof of eligibility. Ask whether staff or local drivers can help with this platform and its assistance system. That support can be more useful to a newcomer than another advertised geometry option that has no clear setup baseline.

Start with a repeatable circle in each direction, then link simple turns without altering multiple settings. Keep the ground clean and observe whether a change in dust or temperature affects consistency before buying hardware. After the session inspect tires, steering movement and debris around the electronics tray. The Readyset is intended to simplify entry, but control practice and maintenance still form part of ownership. We have not established a whole-car water-use claim here; a dry predictable surface is also the more useful environment for learning drift behavior.

sections.heading: Body and service: Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red
paragraphs: The Lightning Red Toyota86 body is finished and uses Kyosho’s Ultra Scale Body Plus arrangement, avoiding conventional visible drilled mounting holes. That is a genuine convenience for the buyer who wants a handsome car without trimming and painting a shell. The GT86 front, mirrors, body shape and light buckets also make the exact variant more attractive than a body-less chassis price might suggest.

Light buckets do not mean LEDs are included. If illuminated detail appeals, check the model’s supported light equipment and its separate cost. Avoid letting a promotional photograph with lights dictate the first-session shopping list. The needed purchases are battery, charger and transmitter cells; cosmetic electronics can wait until the car is functioning and the body-removal procedure is familiar.

The manufacturer lists 441 mm length, 208 mm width and 136 mm height. Its body-off photograph in our gallery shows the actual drift layout, with another whole-car view showing the finished Toyota. These are credited official images rather than photographs of a test car owned by us. Protect the exposed mirrors and body details when carrying the vehicle and practicing near walls. The hidden mounting system is useful only if you learn its release procedure and keep wiring clear of it; forcing the shell because a lead was trapped defeats the convenience it was intended to provide.

sections.heading: Startup basket: Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red
paragraphs: The directly verified Tower Hobbies exact KYO34502T1 Readyset listing is $284.99 at this check and marked in stock. This is a dated independent retailer car-only reference, not manufacturer MSRP. It differs from an older indexed Kyosho America $245.99 reference, so this review uses the directly verified retailer amount rather than silently treating the cached figure as a live price. The exact Amazon link remains separate and its live offer expires from display. Battery, charger, transmitter cells and any venue-required tires still need their own prices.

The essential basket adds four AA transmitter cells, an appropriate drive pack and matching charger. Kyosho’s product page names 7.2 V NiMH options, including SPEED HOUSE 71322C or 71324B packs and suitable listed chargers, but current USD prices for those exact accessories were not verified here. The complete basket therefore has a real equipment list without an invented subtotal. Check the installed connector and controller requirements when considering equipment you already own.

Optional lights, different tires required by a venue and electronics changes belong in separate budget lines. If the plan already calls for sensored brushless power, a new radio and another gyro, compare a complete car supplied closer to that requirement. The D2’s value rests partly on its coordinated stock installation. Buying the whole Readyset solely to keep the shell can be an enjoyable personal project, but it is a different financial case from the first-drift recommendation. I would settle the power equipment and venue tire first, then let practice identify whether anything else needs changing.

sections.heading: Real alternatives: Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red
paragraphs: The Traxxas 4-Tec Drift Nissan 240SX is a complete RTR alternative with its own steering-and-throttle assistance, supplied tire options and a finished S13 body. It also needs battery and charging equipment. Consider it when the body and documented Traxxas control system suit your preferences. We have not performed a common-surface comparison and do not claim that the two assistance systems deliver identical behavior.

An MST RMX 2.5 RTR brushless is a relevant complete-car route for someone who wants a brushless RWD package from the outset. Verify the exact body, gyro, servo and local completion contents, because the RMX name also covers kits and different electronics versions. A low bare-chassis price is not a fair substitute for a complete-car comparison. Put the battery, charger and tire requirements beside the vehicle price for each option.

The D2 AE86 Readyset offers another body on the drift platform. Choose that Toyota subject when it is the thing you want to own, but confirm the precise regional package rather than assuming every release uses identical electronics. I would keep the red Toyota86 on a first casual-drift shortlist because the finished coupe and integrated assistance form a clear stock package. For regular tandem sessions, let the venue’s recommendations narrow the alternatives before comparing feature counts. The car is more useful when the local floor and support suit it than when its specification simply looks longer than a rival’s.

sections.heading: Buying verdict: Fazer D2 Toyota 86 GT Tuned Lightning Red
paragraphs: The Toyota86 D2 earns a recommendation for a casual first RWD drifter who wants the body and basic electronics coordinated. The stock G22 motor, dedicated servo, receiver/gyro and finished hidden-mount shell form an understandable purchase. Its reservations are separate power equipment, venue-dependent tires and the possibility that a buyer already committed to another electronics system would immediately replace much of the package they paid for.

Our five editorial categories assess entry completeness, drift-specific equipment, documented adjustment, service planning and complete-purchase value for that buyer. No measured slide consistency, steering speed, top speed, impact resistance or reliability result is assigned. The independent release coverage is clearly labeled as announcement context and its regional suffix is retained. The manufacturer establishes the mechanism; the API establishes the exact T1 listing and offer.

I would choose the car when you want to spend the first sessions learning the stock controls on smooth ground, with the red Toyota body already finished. Confirm battery compatibility, note the baseline assistance settings and ask the venue about tires before spending on options. I would skip it for rough-ground use or an upgrade plan that already removes its main stock equipment. For the named beginner, the D2 is a coherent way to start a drifting project, provided the practice floor and complete budget receive the same attention as the attractive GT86 shell.
